chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani, Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hashem al-Mokattib, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya - the friend of al-Sabiri - who said:

Abu Qorrah - a friend of al-Jaseliq (the Catholic Archbishop) - asked me to take him to Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him). I requested permission to do so. Then the Imam (peace be upon him) said, ‘Bring him in.’ Then when Abu Qorrah entered, he kissed the rug beneath the Imam’s (peace be upon him) feet and said, ‘This is how our religion has instructed us to treat the noble ones of our era.’

Then he said to him, ‘May God keep you healthy. What is your opinion about one group who has a claim and another group that are known to be just and acknowledge their claim?’ The Imam (peace be upon him) said, ‘Their claim is right.’

Then Abu Qorrah asked, ‘What about another group who have a claim, but they cannot find any witnesses to prove their claim other than themselves?’ The Imam (peace be upon him) replied, ‘Their claim is rejected.’

Abu Qorrah said, ‘Now we claim that Jesus is the Spirit of God and His Word. The Muslims agree with us regarding this claim. However, the Muslims claim that Muhammad is a Prophet of God, but we do not acknowledge their claim. Therefore what both groups agree upon is better than what they disagree upon.’
Then Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him) asked him, ‘What is your name?’ He said, ‘John.’

The Imam (peace be upon him) replied, ‘O John! We believe in Jesus (peace be upon him) - the Spirit of God and His Word - who believed in Muhammad (peace be upon him), gave the glad tidings of his coming, and confessed that he was a servant who has a Lord.’

Then if the Jesus in whom you believe is not so, and he does not believe in Muhammad (peace be upon him) and does not believe in being a servant of God and does not accept God the Honorable the Exalted to be his Lord, then we reject such a Jesus. Then how could we reject him and you claim that we agree with each other?
Then (John) Abu Qorrah stood up and told me (i.e. Safwan ibn Yahya), ‘Stand up. This meeting was not beneficial for us.’

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha
key_terms.الْجَاثَلِيق: Al-Jaseliq, a title for the Catholic Archbishop
key_terms.عَبْدٌ مَرْبُوبٌ: A servant who has a Lord

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ar-Ridha refute the Christian claim that Muslims and Christians disagree on the core tenets of faith?
ai.summary: This dialogue, recorded in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, highlights Imam al-Rida’s (AS) method of engaging Christian scholars by deconstructing their theological premises regarding Jesus (AS). He demonstrates that the 'Spirit and Word' of God they revere is identical to the Jesus who testified to Muhammad’s prophethood, thereby turning their argument for common ground into a proof for Islamic monotheism. The encounter concludes with the scholar’s departure, illustrating the intellectual superiority of the Imam’s reasoning in interfaith discourse.
